comparison.objective: Candidate commissions a shock absorber by unlocking, tuning, relocking, and validating repeated dynamic stops; pr-1904 measures voltage by simultaneously placing two probes on specified terminals.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key engagement, counterholding, fine collar rotation, torque-limited locking, control actuation, and response-guided iteration. pr-1904 requires bimanual probe pickup, precise insertion into two small openings, and simultaneous steady holding. Tool insertion is shared generically, but the tested manipulation abilities differ meaningfully.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two safe physical carriage cycles within stroke, energy, velocity, rebound, overload, hard-stop, and lock-retention constraints. pr-1904 requires both held probes to contact L/N for 1 second, with zero score for entering another opening. Candidate leaves collar-drift tolerance, excessive-rebound threshold, overload threshold, and witness torque numerically undeclared; pr-1904 specifies insertion depths and timing, though some electrical behavior is pose-derived. These omissions do not create plausible duplication.
comparison.reason: All four available pr-1904 spec versions were read. They consistently test simultaneous electrical probing, whereas the candidate tests mechanical damper adjustment, retention, and resulting dynamic energy absorption. The objectives, central force/coordination sequence, and full-score outcomes are materially different.
